hero.name: Mehul Singh.
hero.description: I build systems from first principles. My work spans computational architectures, systems engineering, and high-performance computing.

evolves.title: Research Sandbox (evolves.cc)

about.text: I am a systems researcher and engineer driven by a fundamental need to understand how things work at their core. Rather than assembling off-the-shelf components, I deconstruct problems to their base assumptions, focusing on structural elegance, mathematical correctness, and computational efficiency. My cross-domain approach bridges physical system behavior with software architecture, allowing me to conceptualize and build robust systems characterized by deep analytical maturity and rigorous validation.

projects.title: Next-Gen Operating System (In Progress)
projects.desc: I founded and am spearheading a long-term, open-source initiative to architect and build a custom, secure-by-design operating system from scratch. As the lead systems engineer, I design the core kernel internals, preemptive thread scheduling, and low-level memory management for high-performance, bare-metal execution. Beyond core development, I drive the project's long-term research vision, focusing on next-generation computing concepts like hardware-agnostic portability and AI-assisted resource allocation.

projects.title: BBRES-RNG: Scheduler-Based Entropy Engine
projects.desc: I architected a scheduler-based entropy engine that utilizes OS thread-scheduling nondeterminism to produce high-quality entropy for PRNG/CSPRNG seeding. The system supports 32x32 concurrent thread-segment execution and features modular entropy collection, bit mixing, and bounded random number generation. It achieved a near-perfect 7.999952/8.0 Shannon entropy and demonstrated exceptional statistical robustness against NIST SP 800-22 and adversarial machine learning attacks.

projects.title: Zero-Copy Segmented Commit Log
projects.desc: I engineered a high-throughput segmented commit log designed for concurrent appends, crash recovery, and persistent storage. By minimizing synchronization overhead, the system achieved a processing rate of over 4.39 million messages per second across four concurrent producer threads. I also implemented scalable segment lifecycle management, ensuring automatic creation, rollover, and recovery for a production-ready storage solution.

projects.title: Archiver
projects.desc: I architected a custom binary archive format featuring recursive directory packaging, metadata preservation, and CRC32 integrity verification. To optimize performance, I engineered a streaming archive engine that enables the scalable, memory-efficient processing of large files and nested directories. Furthermore, I developed a pluggable compression framework utilizing the Strategy Pattern to seamlessly integrate Huffman and LZW compression algorithms.

projects.title: MEDMSII: A character Encoding/Decoding Tool
projects.desc: Built a lightweight text obfuscation tool in Java that maps characters to custom binary codes, injects randomized noise bits, and applies a bitwise complement for scrambling, paired with a decoder that exactly reverses each step. A hands-on exploration of binary representation and building invertible algorithms.

projects.title: Vointhez
projects.desc: Authored a whitepaper proposing a new phonetic segmentation method for text-to-speech: splitting words into two-character pronunciation units via exhaustive lookup tables (676 letter-pair combinations, plus numeral and symbol libraries).

experience.desc: Built a domain-specific tokenizer for mining and geological text as part of applied NLP research. Optimized tokenization algorithms to handle technical vocabulary heavily underrepresented in standard text corpora.

Undergraduate studies with a heavy independent research focus on AI systems, NLP, and computational foundations. Recognized among the top tier for research potential and analytical execution. Dean's List 2024, Student Excellence Award 2025.
